moved.sentence: All components MUST integrate with platform accessibility APIs from initial implementation:

judged.note: Rule must-integrate-accessibility-apis-from-day-one keeps the MUST, its scope (all components) and timing (from initial implementation), and says the rules that follow are that integration's requirements, as the old list lead-in did.

moved.sentence: Semantic roles and labels on all interactive elements

judged.note: Rule must-give-interactive-elements-semantic-roles-and-labels keeps the list item at MUST, the level of the list's MUST lead-in, for all interactive elements.

moved.sentence: VoiceOver (Apple) / TalkBack (Android) / screen reader (Web) full support

judged.note: Rule must-fully-support-screen-readers keeps full screen reader support at MUST for VoiceOver (Apple), TalkBack (Android) and web screen readers via ARIA, and adds Narrator (Windows).

moved.sentence: Keyboard and switch control navigation

judged.note: Rule must-support-keyboard-and-switch-control keeps both keyboard and switch control navigation at MUST.

moved.sentence: WCAG AA minimum contrast (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text)

judged.note: Rule must-meet-wcag-aa-contrast keeps WCAG AA minimum contrast at MUST with both ratios (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text).

moved.sentence: Meaningful focus order following visual layout

judged.note: Rule must-follow-visual-layout-focus-order keeps a meaningful focus order that follows visual layout at MUST.

moved.sentence: # Respect accessibility display options

judged.note: The heading's instruction survives in must-respond-to-display-settings, which ends 'they respect accessibility display options', at MUST.

moved.sentence: # Accessibility

judged.note: The '# Accessibility' heading carried no requirement; it titled a second copy of the requirement list. The intro keeps the topic heading ('# Accessibility from day one') with a framing line, and the list's content lives in the All platforms rules.

moved.sentence: Requirements:

judged.note: The 'Requirements:' lead-in survives in must-integrate-accessibility-apis-from-day-one, which says the requirements of that integration are the rules that follow.

moved.sentence: Screen reader full support (VoiceOver, TalkBack, Narrator, ARIA)

judged.note: Rule must-fully-support-screen-readers keeps full screen reader support at MUST for all four named readers: VoiceOver, TalkBack, Narrator and ARIA-based web readers.

moved.sentence: Components MUST respond to platform accessibility and display settings including reduced motion, high contrast, color inversion, bold text, and grayscale

judged.note: Rule must-respond-to-display-settings keeps the MUST and all five named settings: reduced motion, high contrast, color inversion, bold text and grayscale.

moved.sentence: Components MUST respond to these Android accessibility settings:

judged.note: Rule must-respond-to-android-accessibility-settings, under Kotlin, keeps the MUST, names all eight Android settings and points to the Kotlin table, which still gives each setting's API and action.

moved.sentence: Components MUST respond to these SwiftUI environment values:

judged.note: Rule must-respond-to-swiftui-environment-values, under Swift, keeps the MUST, names all six SwiftUI settings and points to the Swift table, which still gives each setting's key and action.

moved.sentence: [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) — minimum AA conformance for all components.

judged.note: Rule should-meet-wcag-2-2-aa keeps the unkeyed standard at SHOULD (minimum AA conformance for all web components, the old typescript part's scope), and the WCAG 2.2 link is in references.

moved.sentence: WCAG 2.2 is the current W3C Recommendation and supersedes 2.1; honor its new AA criteria: focus not obscured, focus appearance, a single-pointer alternative to dragging movements, **target size minimum 24×24 CSS px** (reconcile with the 44pt target in [adc.guideline.implementing.ui.touch-click-targets](cookbook:73b254b4-c611-434a-a9f4-67c8a7155576) — 44pt is the stricter Apple guidance), consistent help, redundant entry, and accessible authentication (no cognitive-function test).

judged.note: should-meet-wcag-2-2-aa keeps 'current W3C Recommendation and supersedes 2.1'. should-honor-wcag-2-2-new-aa-criteria keeps, at SHOULD, every new AA criterion, including the 24x24 CSS px target and the reconciliation with the 44pt touch-click-targets guidance.

moved.sentence: Treat WCAG 3.0 as a horizon Working Draft, not yet actionable.

judged.note: Rule should-treat-wcag-3-as-not-yet-actionable keeps the instruction at SHOULD, with WCAG 3.0 still described as a horizon Working Draft that is not yet actionable.

moved.sentence: [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/) — correct ARIA roles, states, and properties.

judged.note: Rule should-follow-wai-aria-authoring-practices keeps correct ARIA roles, states and properties at SHOULD, and the link is in references.

moved.sentence: Components MUST respond to these user preferences:

judged.note: Rule must-respond-to-css-user-preferences keeps the MUST for web components, names all six media-query preferences and points to the TypeScript table, which still gives each query and action.

moved.sentence: Screen reader support: use ARIA roles, `aria-live` for dynamic content, proper landmark regions.

judged.note: Rule should-support-screen-readers-with-aria keeps all three techniques at SHOULD for web: ARIA roles, aria-live for dynamic content and landmark regions.

moved.sentence: Set `AutomationProperties.Name` on interactive elements that lack visible text labels.

judged.note: Rule should-set-automation-name-on-unlabeled-elements, under Windows, keeps the unkeyed instruction at SHOULD with its condition (elements that lack visible text labels).

moved.sentence: Use `AutomationProperties.LabeledBy` for form fields

judged.note: Rule should-use-labeled-by-for-form-fields, under Windows, keeps AutomationProperties.LabeledBy for form fields at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Use `AutomationProperties.LiveSetting` for dynamic content regions

judged.note: Rule should-use-live-setting-for-dynamic-regions, under Windows, keeps AutomationProperties.LiveSetting for dynamic content regions at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: High contrast support is automatic when using `ThemeResource` — never hard-code colors

judged.note: Rule must-not-hard-code-colors keeps the fact that ThemeResource makes high contrast automatic, and raises 'never hard-code colors' to MUST NOT.

moved.sentence: Test with [Accessibility Insights for Windows](https://accessibilityinsights.io/)

judged.note: Rule should-test-with-accessibility-insights keeps testing with Accessibility Insights for Windows at SHOULD, link included.

moved.sentence: Keyboard navigation: all interactive elements must be reachable via Tab, actionable via Enter/Space

judged.note: Rule must-make-elements-keyboard-reachable raises the lowercase 'must' to MUST: every interactive element reachable via Tab and actionable via Enter/Space.

moved.sentence: Components MUST respond to these Windows accessibility settings:

judged.note: Rule must-respond-to-windows-accessibility-settings keeps the MUST, names all eight Windows settings and points to the Windows table, which still gives each setting's detection API and action.

moved.sentence: Components MUST respond to platform accessibility and display settings including reduced motion, high contrast, color inversion, bold text, and grayscale.

judged.note: Rule must-respond-to-display-settings keeps this sentence's MUST and all five settings: reduced motion, high contrast, color inversion, bold text and grayscale.

moved.sentence: All components MUST integrate with platform accessibility APIs from initial implementation.

judged.note: Rule must-integrate-accessibility-apis-from-day-one keeps the MUST, the scope (all components) and the timing (from initial implementation), and, like the old 'Requirements:' lead-in, says the rules that follow are that integration's requirements.
